verdicts.claim: [0] The .data {name,thunk,impl} record routes around the coverage-blocked page 0x5456000; AuthPlayerEnterWorldAttachedToRidable impl = 0x55CD510, present in all 3 images.
verdicts.reasoning: Reproduced independently. `fkdis.py cov 0x5456000 0x1000` = `page 0x05456000 ZERO` in s129, merged2 AND tuthero [M]. `strxref native` gives name rva 0x8A4E428 / thunk 0x5456380 [M]. I re-read the 24 raw bytes at .data 0x9C1E5B8 myself: `28e411c1f77f0000 8063b2bdf77f0000 10d5c9bdf77f0000` -> VAs 0x7FF7C111E428 / 0x7FF7BDB26380 / 0x7FF7BDC9D510, which against ImageBase 0x7FF7B86D0000 (read from the PE header, not retyped) give rva 0x8A4E428 / 0x5456380 / 0x55CD510 [M]. `cov 0x55CD510` = present in all three [M]. I also confirmed the record table is structurally real rather than an accidental triple: my own independent .data sweep found 16,279 such records (unit: records) and 14,689 of 16,278 adjacent pairs sit at a uniform stride of 72 bytes, sorted alphabetically by name [M].
verdicts.correction: Substance stands; the NOVELTY framing does not. This instrument and this exact criticism are already in the repo. `docs/fk1-stub-claim-recheck.md` section 2 documents the same 3-field .data record {NameUTF8, execThunk, implPtr}. `docs/fk22-dropphase-reachability.md:579` and :675 already say a sibling verdict was mis-filed COVERAGE-BLOCKED and that the identical .data triple yields a real impl, i.e. apply your own resolution method to your own negative. And :123 already names 0x055cd510 and already observes it begins test rdx,rdx / je. So this is a correct application of a method the repo already held, not a new route.

verdicts.reasoning: The POSITIVE half reproduces exactly and independently. My own record scan gives SpawnPlayer rec=0x9bdb230/thunk=0x534c070/impl=0xf7eb50; OverridePlaneLocations rec=0x9bd4b08; AuthSetSpawnTeamLeader rec=0x9c14fa0; SetDropLeader rec=0x9c29f50 - byte-identical to the table at fk1-stub-claim-recheck.md:271-277 [M]. GoToPhase rec=0x9c1f298/0x5457200/0x5601020 and BP_AuthSetCurrentPhase 0x53878d0/0x567a160 [M]. Both thunk-tail derivations reproduce: SetPilotPlayerState thunk 0x53375E0 -> 0x5337650 `e88be32a00` call 0x7ff7bdcb59e0 = rva 0x55E59E0 == record impl [M]; AddTeamDropEvent thunk 0x5463350 -> 0x546344F `e88cb61100` call 0x7ff7bdc4eae0 = rva 0x557EAE0 == record impl == the value at fk22:138 [M]. I byte-searched the raw files: SpawnDropPodForTeam, StartPodGameplay, InitializeDropPod, GetPilotPlayerState occur ascii=0, utf16=0 in s129, merged2 AND tuthero [M] (controls: AuthPlayerEnterWorldAttachedToRidable ascii=1/utf16=2, GoToPhase ascii=1). (b) 'Validated in BOTH directions' overstates: my scale test shows +0x10 is not always the code that runs. verdicts.claim: [12] Patching the stripped getter 0xF7EB50 is categorically ruled out: it is a shared fold with 74/83 call sites, and it is a .text write.

My unaligned .text E8/E9 sweep gives 0xF7EB50 = 71 call + 3 jmp = 74 in s129 and 80 + 3 = 83 in merged2 [M], so a patch would alter 73 other call sites in s129. The .text-write hazard figure is quoted from this repo's own measured A/B (standing .text 10/10 vs 3/36, Fisher p=0.00000008) and is not a claim this session needs to re-derive. verdicts.correction: No correction. This is the best-graded claim in the set - the one place where an [I] label is used correctly, with the reason for the downgrade stated.

summary:
Adversarial re-verification of 13 claims against dumps/s129-poolgate, dumps/merged2 and dumps/tutorial-hero, using an independently written PE loader, .data record enumerator, capstone branch sweep, unaligned rel32 scanner and unwind-chain resolver (I did not trust recs.py, revmap.py or implof.py).

VERDICTS: 7 CONFIRMED ([0],[2],[4],[5],[8],[10],[12]), 5 DOWNGRADE ([1],[3],[6],[9],[11]), 1 REFUTED ([7]).

The core finding survives intact and is now better supported than as filed. AuthPlayerEnterWorldAttachedToRidable's impl really is rva 0x55CD510; at 0x55CD572 it calls the stripped fold 0xF7EB50 (`33 c0 c3`) and unconditionally takes `je 0x55CD7B2` into a "failed to get the round game mode" bail. I added two confirmations the agent did not have: the CHAINED UNWIND INFO proves 0x55CD5A5 and 0x55CD7B2 both chain to primary 0x55CD510 (same function, so the bail block is not a neighbour's), and the error string names the function itself — a name-independent check on the record instrument. I also confirmed zero aligned qword pointers into the dead region, closing the indirect-entry hole a rel32-only scan leaves open.

THE ONE REFUTATION — [7]: "AuthSetSpawnTeamLeader only feeds ALokiDropShip::GetTeamDropLeader" is false. Its flag's reader `IsSpawnTeamLeader` is called from three Angelscript sites, and one of them is `ALokiDropPod::QueueCrewForPodSpawn` (LokiDropPod.as.txt:3752), which IS on the route — InitializeDropPod calls it whenever bIsTeamLeaderPod is true, and SpawnDropPodForTeam passes true. The conclusion survives only under an unstated bIsTeamLeaderPod=false assumption. This is the same incomplete-enumeration error fk22:123 already recorded against a previous agent on this exact function family.

THE FOLD TRAP FIRED ONCE — [9]: "SetOwner impl 0x3375780 REAL" names a 3-way ICF fold after one caller. Three records share that RVA (GetCastRange, OnRep_KnockbackResistCoefficient, SetOwner), it has 3 aligned qword pointers image-wide, and its bytes are `mov rax,[rcx]; jmp [rax+0x538]` — a shared virtual-dispatch tail-jmp, not AActor::SetOwner's body.

THE NEGATIVE CONTROL IS DEGENERATE — [1]/[11]: I measured that Angelscript function names have ZERO byte occurrences (ascii and utf16) in all three images, against native controls reading 1-2. So "AS functions have NO record" is a tautology of a name-keyed scan, not evidence about the record table. Two claims lean on it.

EXTENT ERROR — [3]: the function's true extent from chained .pdata is 0x55CD510..0x55CD5A5 + ..0x55CD77B + 0x55CD7B2..0x55CD7FA; the assumed [.., 0x55CD794) under-scans by 0x66 bytes. I re-ran at the true extent in all three images and still got 0, so the conclusion survives — by luck, not by design. Also three LIVE-source edges do enter the stated interval (0x55cd513/0x55cd548/0x55cd555 -> the ret/epilogue), so "no other branch enters it" is false as written; the true dead span is [0x55CD580,0x55CD77B).

PROVENANCE — [0]: the .data triple instrument, and the exact criticism that a coverage-blocked thunk should be resolved through it, are ALREADY in the repo (fk1-stub-claim-recheck.md §2; fk22 lines 579 and 675), and fk22:123 already names 0x055cd510. Correct application of an existing method, not a new route.

INCIDENTAL, MATTERS FOR FUTURE WORK: merged2 is NOT a superset of s129 — 0xB9E1F0 has 96 rel32 call sites in s129 vs 95 in merged2, so s129 holds decrypted .text pages merged2 lacks. Do not treat merged2 as covering it.

Every load-bearing byte quoted above was re-read from the image this session; every rel32 and rip-relative target was machine-resolved, never retyped.
